'''John Paul''' (25 April 1922{{snd}}27 June 1994) was a biomedical research scientist living in Scotland, UK.  He was the founding director of the [[Beatson Institute for Cancer Research]] in Glasgow, Scotland.<ref name="award">{{Cite web |title=John Paul Career Award |url=https://www.crukscotlandinstitute.ac.uk/cruk-si-education/phd-students/john-paul-career-award.html |publisher=[[Cancer Research UK]]|access-date=9 April 2024 |website=www.crukscotlandinstitute.ac.uk}}</ref>

He wrote five books on the subject of cell biology, tissue culture and cancer, including '' Cell Biology: A Current Summary''<ref>Reviews of ''Cell Biology'':
*Courtney T. Wemyss (1965), "Molecular Biology: A Summary", ''Science'', {{doi|10.1126/science.148.3676.1452}}, {{JSTOR|1716543}}
*Edith K. MacRae (1966), ''The American Biology Teacher'', {{JSTOR|4441476}}
*R. W. Merriam (1967), ''The Quarterly Review of Biology'', {{JSTOR|2820460}}
</ref> and ''Cell and Tissue Culture''.<ref>Reviews of ''Cell and Tissue Culture'':

*Roy Cameron (1959), ''The British Medical Journal'', {{JSTOR|25388296}}
*Margaret R. Murray (1960), ''American Scientist'', {{JSTOR|27827546}}
*Kenneth M. Richter (1961), ''Bios'', {{JSTOR|4606311}}
*''Journal of Medical Education'' (1961), [https://journals.lww.com/academicmedicine/citation/1961/05000/cell_and_tissue_culture.43.aspx]
*''Canadian Journal of Public Health'' (1962), {{JSTOR|41982774}}
*Elli Kohen (1966), ''The Quarterly Review of Biology'', {{JSTOR|2818837}}
*Joshua R. C. Brown (1971), ''Transactions of the American Microscopical Society'', {{JSTOR|3225043}}
</ref>

In 1961 he invented and patented an apparatus for cell and tissue culture.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Apparatus for culture of biological cells and tissues |url=https://patents.google.com/patent/US2975553/en |publisher=[[Google Patents]] |website=patents.google.com |access-date=9 April 2024}}</ref> In 1966, he, along with [[Robert Edwards (physiologist)|Robert Edwards]], derived the world’s first [[embryonic stem cell]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Johnson |first=Martin |title=Robert Edwards: the path to IVF |journal=Reproductive Biomedicine Online |date=2011 |volume=23 |issue=2 |pages=245–262 |doi=10.1016/j.rbmo.2011.04.010 |pmid=21680248 |pmc=3171154 }}</ref>

==Early life and education== 
Paul was born on 25 April 1922 in [[Wishaw]], Lanarkshire, Scotland.<ref name="BMJ">{{cite journal |department=Obituaries|title=J. Paul PHD, FRCPED, FRCPGLAS, FRCPATH, FIBIOL, FRSE|first=Alistair |last=Riddell |doi=10.1136/bmj.309.6968.1577 |journal=[[BMJ]] |year=1994 |volume=309 |issue=1577|pages=1577–1578 |jstor=29725757}}</ref> He graduated from the [[University of Glasgow]] with an MB ChB in 1944, then completed a PhD in biochemistry. He was the Ure scholar at Glasgow University in 1948–51 and the McCunn scholar at the [[University of Edinburgh]], followed by a research fellowship (Rockefeller travelling research fellowship) at the [[Columbia University College of Physicians and Surgeons]] in New York in 1952–53.<ref name="ind">{{Cite news |date=1 July 1994 |title=Obituary: Dr John Paul |author=R. I. Freshney |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/obituary-dr-john-paul-1411175.html |access-date=9 April 2024 |work=[[The Independent]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==
He was director of the Tissue Culture Laboratories of the Department of Biochemistry in the University of Glasgow<ref name="her">{{Cite news |date=30 June 1994 |title=John Paul |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/news/12737647.john-paul/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=9 April 2024 |work=The Herald |language=en}}</ref> and became a reader in 1962 and a Titular Professor in 1964.<ref name="ind" />  He left Glasgow University in 1966 to become Director of the Cancer Research Laboratories of the [[Beatson West of Scotland Cancer Centre|Royal Beatson Memorial Hospital]] in Glasgow.<ref>{{Cite web |title=History of the Beatson |url=https://www.beatson.scot.nhs.uk/about-us/history-of-the-beatson/ |access-date=9 April 2024 | publisher=[[Beatson West of Scotland Cancer Centre]] |website=www.beatson.scot.nhs.uk}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Currie |first1=Alastair |title=The Beatson Institute for Cancer Research and Dr John Paul |journal=The British Journal of Cancer |date=December 1988 |volume=9 |issue=9 |pages=2–3 |pmc=2149102 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=5xJBAAAAIBAJ&pg=6272%2C2106319 |title=End of an era at cancer care centre |first=Rosemary |last=Long |work=[[Evening Times]] |date=11 April 1980 |page=12 |access-date=21 July 2024}}</ref>

He retired in 1987 and died 27 June 1994.<ref name="ind" />

==Awards and honours==
Paul was awarded an honorary DSc by the University of Glasgow in 1989.<ref name="BMJ"/>

There is a John Paul Career Award named after him, for which third year PhD students at the Scotland Institute are eligible .<ref name="award" />
